theory.overview: Mathematical algorithms and prime number theory are fundamental in computer science. Topics include GCD, LCM, modular arithmetic, prime testing, prime factorization, sieve of Eratosthenes, and number theory. Used in cryptography, hashing, and competitive programming. This chapter covers essential math algorithms and prime number techniques.

sections.title: GCD and LCM
sections.content: GCD (Greatest Common Divisor): largest number dividing both. Euclidean algorithm: gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a mod b). Time: $O(\log(\min(a,b)))$. LCM (Least Common Multiple): smallest number divisible by both. lcm(a,b) = a × b / gcd(a,b). Used for fraction simplification and periodicity.

sections.title: Prime Testing
sections.content: Trial division: check divisibility up to $\sqrt{n}$. Time: $O(\sqrt{n})$. Miller-Rabin: probabilistic primality test. Time: $O(k \log^3 n)$ where k is iterations. Deterministic for n < 2^64 with specific bases. Used in cryptography.

sections.title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
sections.content: Find all primes up to n. Mark multiples of each prime starting from 2. Time: $O(n \log \log n)$. Space: $O(n)$. Optimizations: start from p², only odd numbers, segmented sieve for large n. Used for prime generation and factorization.
sections.algorithm: Initialize boolean array. For p from 2 to √n: if prime, mark multiples as composite.

sections.title: Modular Arithmetic
sections.content: Operations modulo m: (a + b) mod m = (a mod m + b mod m) mod m. Similar for subtraction and multiplication. Modular inverse: a⁻¹ mod m exists if gcd(a,m) = 1. Extended Euclidean algorithm finds inverse. Used in cryptography and hashing.

sections.title: Prime Factorization
sections.content: Factor n into prime factors. Trial division up to √n. After trial division, if n > 1, n is prime. Time: $O(\sqrt{n})$. For large n, use Pollard's Rho algorithm. Used in RSA and number theory problems.
sections.algorithm: Divide by smallest prime repeatedly, move to next prime. Continue until n = 1.

keyConcepts.name: Euclidean Algorithm
keyConcepts.description: Efficient GCD computation. gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a mod b). Base case: gcd(a,0) = a.

keyConcepts.name: Sieve
keyConcepts.description: Mark multiples of primes to find all primes up to n. Efficient for bulk prime generation.
keyConcepts.optimization: Start from p², only odd numbers

keyConcepts.name: Modular Inverse
keyConcepts.description: a⁻¹ mod m such that a × a⁻¹ ≡ 1 (mod m). Exists iff gcd(a,m) = 1. Found via extended Euclidean.

keyConcepts.name: Coprime
keyConcepts.description: Two numbers are coprime if gcd(a,b) = 1. Important for modular inverse and Chinese Remainder Theorem.

steps.title: GCD
steps.code: def gcd(a, b): while b: a, b = b, a % b; return a;

steps.title: LCM
steps.code: def lcm(a, b): return a * b // gcd(a, b);

steps.title: Sieve
steps.description: Generate primes up to n using sieve.
steps.code: is_prime = [True] * (n+1); is_prime[0] = is_prime[1] = False; for p in range(2, int(n**0.5)+1): if is_prime[p]: for multiple in range(p*p, n+1, p): is_prime[multiple] = False;

steps.title: Prime Test
steps.description: Check if n is prime using trial division or Miller-Rabin.
steps.code: def is_prime(n): if n < 2: return False; for i in range(2, int(n**0.5)+1): if n % i == 0: return False; return True;

steps.title: Factorize
steps.code: factors = []; p = 2; while p * p <= n: if n % p == 0: factors.append(p); n //= p; else: p += 1; if n > 1: factors.append(n);

practiceProblems.title: Count Primes
practiceProblems.description: Count primes less than n.
practiceProblems.solution: Sieve of Eratosthenes. Mark multiples of each prime.

practiceProblems.title: Ugly Number
practiceProblems.description: Check if n is ugly (prime factors only 2,3,5).
practiceProblems.solution: Divide by 2,3,5 repeatedly. If result is 1, ugly.

practiceProblems.title: Happy Number
practiceProblems.description: Check if n is happy (sum of squares of digits eventually 1).
practiceProblems.solution: Use hash set to detect cycle. Sum squares until 1 or cycle.

practiceProblems.title: Power of Three
practiceProblems.description: Check if n is power of 3.
practiceProblems.solution: Divide by 3 repeatedly. Or use log: 3^x = n → x = log₃(n).

practiceProblems.title: Excel Sheet Column Title
practiceProblems.description: Convert column number to Excel title (1→A, 26→Z, 27→AA).
practiceProblems.solution: Base-26 conversion (1-indexed). n-- before conversion.

practiceProblems.title: Factorial Trailing Zeroes
practiceProblems.description: Count trailing zeros in n!.
practiceProblems.solution: Count factors of 5: n//5 + n//25 + n//125 + ...

practiceProblems.title: Add Digits
practiceProblems.description: Add digits of num until single digit.
practiceProblems.solution: Digital root: 1 + (n-1) % 9. Or iterative sum.

practiceProblems.title: Nth Digit
practiceProblems.description: Find nth digit of infinite sequence 123456789101112...
practiceProblems.solution: Find which number range, which number, which digit.
practiceProblems.hints: Find number range, then number, then digit

practiceProblems.title: Fraction to Recurring Decimal
practiceProblems.description: Convert fraction to decimal string (detect repeating part).
practiceProblems.solution: Long division. Use hash map to detect repeating remainders.
practiceProblems.hints: Long division, hash map for remainders

practiceProblems.title: Super Pow
practiceProblems.description: Calculate a^b mod 1337 where b is large (array of digits).
practiceProblems.solution: Modular exponentiation: (a^b mod m) = ((a^(b/10))^10 × a^(b%10)) mod m.

practiceProblems.title: Sqrt(x)
practiceProblems.description: Compute integer square root of x.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on [0, x]. Or Newton's method.

practiceProblems.title: Divide Two Integers
practiceProblems.description: Divide without using multiplication, division, or mod operator.
practiceProblems.solution: Bit manipulation: subtract divisor × 2^k from dividend, add 2^k to result.

practiceProblems.title: Pow(x, n)
practiceProblems.description: Calculate x^n (n can be negative).
practiceProblems.solution: Fast exponentiation: x^n = (x^(n/2))² if n even, x × x^(n-1) if odd.

practiceProblems.title: Integer Break
practiceProblems.description: Maximum product of integers that sum to n (at least 2 positive integers).
practiceProblems.solution: DP or math: maximize 3s. If n % 3 == 1, use 2+2 instead of 3+1.

practiceProblems.title: Perfect Squares
practiceProblems.description: Least perfect square numbers that sum to n.
practiceProblems.solution: DP. dp[i] = 1 + min(dp[i - j*j]) for all j*j ≤ i.

practiceProblems.title: Sum of Square Numbers
practiceProblems.description: Check if n can be expressed as sum of two squares.
practiceProblems.solution: Two pointers or Fermat's theorem: n = a² + b² iff all prime factors of form (4k+3) have even exponent.

practiceProblems.title: Consecutive Numbers Sum
practiceProblems.description: Number of ways to write n as sum of consecutive positive integers.
practiceProblems.solution: For length k, check if n - k(k-1)/2 is positive and divisible by k.

practiceProblems.title: Bulb Switcher
practiceProblems.description: Bulbs on after n rounds (round i: toggle multiples of i).
practiceProblems.solution: Bulb i is on if i has odd number of divisors (perfect square). Count perfect squares ≤ n.

practiceProblems.title: Nth Magical Number
practiceProblems.description: Nth number divisible by a or b.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search. Count numbers divisible by a or b ≤ mid using inclusion-exclusion.

practiceProblems.title: K-th Smallest in Lexicographical Order
practiceProblems.description: Find kth number in lexicographical order from 1 to n.
practiceProblems.solution: Treat as 10-ary tree. Count nodes in subtree, move to appropriate child.

practiceProblems.title: Reaching Points
practiceProblems.description: Check if can reach (sx, sy) from (tx, ty) with moves: (x, y) → (x+y, y) or (x, x+y).
practiceProblems.solution: Work backwards from target. If tx > ty, tx -= ty (if divisible) or tx = tx % ty. Check if can reach (sx, sy).

practiceProblems.title: K-th Prime Fraction
practiceProblems.description: Find kth smallest fraction formed by arr[i]/arr[j] where i < j.
practiceProblems.solution: Min-heap of (value, i, j). Initialize with arr[i]/arr[n-1] for all i. Extract k times.

practiceProblems.title: Smallest Good Base
practiceProblems.description: Find smallest base k for which all digits of n in base k are 1.
practiceProblems.solution: Try all possible lengths of 1s. For each length, binary search for base.
practiceProblems.hints: Try each length, binary search base

practiceProblems.title: Largest Palindrome Product
practiceProblems.description: Largest palindrome from product of two n-digit numbers.
practiceProblems.solution: Generate palindromes from largest to smallest, check if can be factored into two n-digit numbers.

practiceProblems.title: Prime Arrangements
practiceProblems.description: Count permutations where prime at prime index (1-indexed).
practiceProblems.solution: Count primes ≤ n. Answer = primes! × (n-primes)! mod 10^9+7.
